public_rationale: Most of the 2024 predictions the post lists match the evidence. Frontier models bunched together: the gap between the top two arena models fell to 0.7% in 2024 (e1). Chinese providers cut LLM prices by up to 97% or made models free (e2). Altman said nothing OpenAI shipped in 2024 was worthy of the GPT-5 name (e3). OpenAI's own SimpleQA work called hallucination an open problem (see the hallucination claim). Census data put AI use below 8% even at the largest firms (e4). The main weak spot is o1. Released in 2024, it raised the AIME score from 12% for GPT-4o to 74–83% (e5). That is a large advance the post does not flag, since its caveat covers only o3. The claim itself says 'by and large, with some caveats', which leaves room for one disputed item. So the claim holds as stated, though the related line that all seven were 'right on the money' overstates it.
limitations: The result depends on reading 'by and large' as most of the predictions holding.
The profits prediction was not checked.
Adoption figures depend on how adoption is measured; survey-based measures show higher use.

public_payload.normalized_proposition: Marcus's 2024 AI predictions have largely held, with some caveats.

statement.excerpt: By and large, with some caveats, the predictions for 2024 made here in this Substack have held strong.
statement.document_title: 25 AI Predictions for 2025, from Marcus on AI

from_speaker: predictions for 2024 made here in this Substack
our_interpretation: The post lists the core 2024 predictions as: many GPT-4 level models; no GPT-5 (no massive advance); a price war; very little moat; no robust solution to hallucinations; limited corporate adoption; modest profits.
Plain reading: most of these predictions matched what happened in 2024. 'By and large, with some caveats' allows a minority of misses or partial misses.
The tweet itself is the speaker's writing. It is used only to define what was predicted, never as evidence of the outcome.
criteria.support_condition: Independent evidence shows that most of the listed predictions held in 2024, with no more than one or two clear misses.
criteria.contradiction_condition: Independent evidence shows that several of the listed predictions clearly failed in 2024, for example a major leap well beyond GPT-4 level across the field, robust hallucination fixes, or broad and deep corporate adoption.

evidence.excerpt: the difference between the top two models shrank from 4.9% in 2023 to just 0.7% in 2024.
evidence.explanation: Frontier models bunched closely together in 2024. That fits the predictions of many similar models and little moat.

evidence.excerpt: On Tuesday, Alibaba cut prices by up to 97% for some of its Qwen LLM models. Hours later, Baidu said its Ernie Speed and Ernie Light, two lighter versions of its Ernie LLM, would be free for all business users.
evidence.explanation: Shows a price war among LLM providers in 2024.

evidence.excerpt: nothing the company is working on now (for 2024) is worthy of the GPT-5 moniker.
The largest size class (250+ employees) exhibits the highest use rate, rising from 5.2% to 7.8% over time
evidence.explanation: Official data show AI used in production by fewer than 8% of even the largest US firms through August 2024. That fits the limited-adoption prediction.

evidence.excerpt: On the 2024 AIME exams, GPT‑4o only solved on average 12% (1.8/15) of problems. o1 averaged 74% (11.1/15) with a single sample per problem
evidence.explanation: o1 was released in 2024 and beat GPT-4o by a wide margin on hard reasoning tests. That strains the 'no massive advance' part of the predictions, and the post flags only o3, not o1.
